prompt: Chain ConstructionOrderLog's constructors with this(...), override describe(), and let the shared log prove the base constructor runs first. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: A constructor always runs its superclass constructor before its own body, so by the time the subclass assigns its fields the base class is already finished. The provided base calls describe() during construction, and because that call is dispatched to the override, the subclass method runs while label is still null -- which is exactly why calling an overridable method from a constructor is a well-known trap. this(log, "default") delegates to the other constructor rather than duplicating its work, and it must be the first statement, so it cannot be combined with an explicit super(...) call.
hints: this(log, "default") has to be the very first statement in the one-argument constructor -- replace the super(log) call, do not add to it.
The two-argument constructor appends its line AFTER assigning the field, so the label appears in the text.
Override describe() with the same protected signature; it reads the label field, which is still null while the base constructor is running.
